params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide that shows you **how to pull a deep dive into a network interface** on the most common platforms and tools. Pick the section that matches your environment (Linux, Windows, macOS, or a virtual appliance) and run the commands. --- ## 1️⃣ Linux – “ip” + “ethtool” + “sysfs” | What you want | Command(s) | Why it’s useful | |---------------|------------|-----------------| | **Basic state & MAC** | `ip link show ` | Shows `UP/DOWN`, MTU, MAC, speed, duplex, flags (PROMISC, ALLMULTI, etc.) | | **All details (flags, stats, etc.)** | `ip -details link show ` | Adds `LOWER_UP`, `RUNNING`, `NOARP`, `DYNAMIC`, `MASTER/SLAVE`, `BROADCAST`, `MULTICAST`, `LOOPBACK` | | **IP addresses & scopes** | `ip -details address show ` | Lists IPv4/IPv6 addresses, prefix lengths, labels, scopes (global, link, host) | | **Routing table** | `ip -details route show` | See which routes point to this interface, metrics, scope, type (unicast, local, broadcast) | | **Neighbor cache** | `ip -details neigh show` | ARP/NDP entries, state (REACHABLE, STALE, DELAY, PROBE, FAILED) | | **Multicast groups** | `ip -details maddr show` | Which multicast addresses the interface has joined | | **Statistics** | `ethtool -S ` | Driver‑level counters (rx/tx packets, errors, collisions, dropped, etc.) | | **Driver & firmware** | `ethtool -i ` | Driver name, firmware version, bus info | | **Feature list** | `ethtool -k ` | Offloads enabled (gro, gso, tso, tx-checksum-ipv4, etc.) | | **Ring buffer sizes** | `ethtool -G rx 4096 tx 4096` | Tune RX/TX ring buffers | | **Promiscuous mode** | `ip link set promisc on/off` | Enable/disable promiscuous mode | | **Sysfs view** | `cat /sys/class/net//address`
`cat /sys/class/net//mtu`
`cat /sys/class/net//operstate` | Low‑level kernel view; handy for scripts | | **Driver logs** | `dmesg | grep ` | See boot‑time or runtime driver messages | ### Quick script to dump everything ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash IFACE=${1:-eth0} echo "=== $IFACE ===" ip -details link show $IFACE ip -details address show $IFACE ip -details route show ip -details neigh show ip -details maddr show ethtool -S $IFACE ethtool -i $IFACE ethtool -k $IFACE ``` Run it as `./dump_iface.sh eth0`. --- ## 2️⃣ Windows – PowerShell + WMI | What you want | Cmdlet | Notes | |---------------|--------|-------| | **Interface list** | `Get-NetAdapter` | Shows status, MAC, speed, duplex, driver | | **Detailed config** | `Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias ""` | IP, DNS, gateway, DHCP status | | **Advanced properties** | `Get-NetAdapterAdvancedProperty -Name ""` | Offloads, VLAN, flow control | | **Statistics** | `Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name ""` | Packets, bytes, errors, discards | | **Driver info** | `Get-WmiObject Win32_NetworkAdapter -Filter "NetConnectionID=''"` | DriverVersion, Manufacturer, PNPDeviceID | | **Event logs** | `Get-WinEvent -LogName System | Where-Object {$_.Message -match ''}` | Driver events, errors | #### Example ```powershell $adap = Get-NetAdapter -Name "Ethernet0" $adap | Format-List * Get-NetIPConfiguration -InterfaceAlias "Ethernet0" | Format-List * Get-NetAdapterStatistics -Name "Ethernet0" | Format-Table * ``` --- ## 3️⃣ macOS – `networksetup` + `ifconfig` | What you want | Command | Why | |---------------|---------|-----| | **Hardware list** | `networksetup -listallhardwareports` | Maps port names to BSD device names (en0, en1) | | **Interface state** | `ifconfig ` | Flags (UP, RUNNING, BROADCAST, MULTICAST, etc.), MTU, MAC | | **IP config** | `ifconfig inet` | IPv4 address, netmask, broadcast | | **IPv6 config** | `ifconfig inet6` | IPv6 address, prefix length | | **Route table** | `netstat -rn` | See which routes use this interface | | **Neighbor cache** | `arp -an` | ARP entries | | **Statistics** | `netstat -i ` | Packets, errors, drops | | **Driver info** | `system_profiler SPNetworkDataType | grep -A5 ""` | Driver, firmware, vendor | | **Promiscuous mode** | `sudo ifconfig promisc` | Enable promiscuous mode | --- ## 4️⃣ Virtual Appliances / Cloud (VMware, Hyper-V, KVM) | Tool | What it gives | How to use | |------|--------------|------------| | **VMware ESXi** | `esxcfg-nics -l` | List VMkernel NICs, status, speed, MTU | | **Hyper‑V** | `Get-NetAdapter -CimSession ` | Remote query of VM's virtual switch adapters | | **KVM** | `virsh domiflist ` | List interfaces attached to a domain | | **Open vSwitch** | `ovs-vsctl list interface ` | Show OVS interface options, statistics | | **Cloud provider CLI** | e.g., `aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces` | Retrieve ENI details, attachment, security groups | --- ## 5️⃣ Cross‑Platform SNMP If the device exposes SNMP: ```bash snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifTable snmpwalk -v2c -c public localhost IF-MIB::ifXTable ``` Fields returned: `ifIndex`, `ifDescr`, `ifType`, `ifMtu`, `ifSpeed`, `ifPhysAddress`, `ifAdminStatus`, `ifOperStatus`, `ifInOctets`, `ifOutOctets`, etc. --- ## 6️⃣ RESTful APIs (for SD‑WAN, NFVI, or custom appliances) Many modern devices expose a JSON API. Example: ```bash curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ https://api.example.com/v1/interfaces/ ``` Typical JSON payload: ```json { "id": "eth0", "mac": "00:11:22:33:44:55", "status": "up", "speed": "1000Mbps", "duplex": "full", "mtu": 1500, "ipv4": { "address": "192.168.1.10", "prefix": 24, "gateway": "192.168.1.1" }, "stats": { "rx_packets": 123456, "tx_packets": 654321, "rx_errors": 12, "tx_errors": 34 } } ``` Use the vendor’s SDK or open‑source libraries (Python `requests`, Go `net/http`) to automate queries. --- ## 7️⃣ Tips for Troubleshooting | Symptom | Check | Command | |---------|-------|---------| | **Link down** | Physical cable, port status | `ethtool ` (check `link detected`) | | **No IP** | DHCP lease, static config | `dhclient -v ` (Linux) / `ip addr flush ; dhclient ` | | **High error counts** | Driver, PHY | `ethtool -S `; `ethtool -i ` | | **Packet loss** | Queue depth, offloads | `ethtool -G rx 8192 tx 8192`; `ethtool -k ` | | **Latency spikes** | Flow control, jumbo frames | `ethtool -K pause on`; `ethtool -G rx 2048 tx 2048` | | **Security audit** | MAC spoofing, VLAN | `ethtool -N vlan 100 ingress` | --- ### Bottom line * **Linux** → `ip` + `ethtool` + `/sys/class/net/…` * **Windows** → PowerShell `Get-NetAdapter` + WMI * **macOS** → `ifconfig` + `networksetup` * **Virtual** → Vendor CLI (`esxcfg-nics`, `virsh`, `ovs-vsctl`) * **SNMP** → `snmpwalk` for standardized MIB data * **REST** → Vendor API for JSON dumps Pick the right toolset for your platform, run the appropriate command, and you’ll have a full picture of the interface’s configuration, status, and performance. Happy troubleshooting!
